snapshot.sha256Note: The SHA-256 of the committed data/prices.json these verdicts were computed from. Yahoo's adjusted closes for dividend payers are not reproducible between fetches, so the committed file - not a fresh fetch - is the reference data. A rerun that reports a different hash is a rerun on different data.

headline: Hypothesis 1 (hidden concentration): not supported on the headline correlation-only test, supported on the registered test. Hypothesis 2 (a tightening market): not supported against RSP, the registered benchmark. Hypothesis 3 (players learn): collecting - no player data exists yet. The two tests disagree, and both are reported. The verdict for Hypothesis 1 is the headline one, "not supported", from the correlation-only ratio R, which holds the weights and the volatilities fixed and so measures correlation alone. Beside it, and reported because it is what was registered rather than because it decides anything, the registered test says "supported", from the registered ratio of effective risk sources to holdings, which also moves with how unevenly the weights spread the money - and that test clears its own 0.60 threshold at 0.523 even on holdings with no correlation at all, so "supported" there is not on its own evidence for the claim. A disagreement is itself a result: it says the two measures are answering different questions, and it is not resolved by choosing the more favourable one.

headline.statistic: the correlation-only ratio R = ENB(w, Sigma) / ENB(w, diag Sigma)
headline.note: The beginner median of 0.773 and the control median of 0.844 are 0.072 apart, less than the 0.100 this page asks for, so this measure has not separated the two sets.
headline.limit: R deliberately ignores weight concentration: holding the weights fixed is exactly how it isolates correlation. A portfolio can score well on R and still be a poor mix, for instance by holding nearly all its money in one name. The registered numbers beside it are what speak to that.

registered.statistic: the registered ratio of effective risk sources to holdings
registered.note: The beginner median of 0.327 and the control median of 0.381 are 0.055 apart, less than the 0.100 this page asks for, so this measure has not separated the two sets.
registered.limit: On holdings that are exactly uncorrelated and exactly equally volatile - where there is no hidden concentration at all - this median still comes out at 0.523, below its own 0.6 threshold. So it is only meaningful to the extent the beginner median falls below that benchmark, not merely below 0.6.

combinations.benchmarkWhy: Reported beside RSP, never the verdict. The AI names are among the largest weights in a cap-weighted S&P 500, so a basket of them correlates with it partly by arithmetic rather than by markets tightening. That is weakness 7 in the PRD, and it is why PREREG.md registered RSP instead.

leaveOneOut.statement: No single basket stock changes a verdict: all 13 reruns agree with the headline.
leaveOneOut.note: Each rerun keeps its verdicts and medians. The full 500-value distributions are reported for the baseline run, under hypothesis1, as PREREG.md asks; of the reruns it asks only whether any single drop flips a verdict.
